subject: Justin Tseng City Council Re-election Platform
overview: Incumbent City Councilor Justin Tseng discussed his first-term legislative record and outlined his priorities for re-election, emphasizing housing zoning reform, municipal finance, and government accessibility.

items.title: Introduction and Personal Background
items.summary: Councilor Tseng introduced himself as a product of Medford Public Schools and the city's first Asian American elected official, noting how his background informs his approach to representation.

items.title: First-Term Reflections
items.summary: The discussion highlighted legislative work on climate action, infrastructure affordability, and efforts to modernize City Council rules for increased accessibility.

items.title: Civic Engagement and Outreach
items.summary: Tseng addressed the challenges of engaging residents without a local newspaper and proposed meeting immigrant communities in their own neighborhoods to gather feedback.

items.title: High School Construction and Municipal Finance
items.summary: The councilor supported the construction of a new high school and detailed the role of the Financial Task Force in managing capital project funding and federal aid expiration.

items.title: Second-Term Priorities and Revenue
items.summary: Future goals include transit-oriented development along Route 16, housing production through zoning reform, and evaluating the necessity of a tax override.

items.title: Pending Ordinances and Inclusion
items.summary: Tseng outlined legislative efforts to establish a Youth Commission, a Gender Equity Commission, and a Welcoming City ordinance to codify non-cooperation with ICE.
